slides.headline: Three brothers swear an oath. Why are the women crying?
slides.sub: Jacques-Louis David, The Oath of the Horatii, 1784

slides.headline: Rome against Alba
slides.text: Ancient Rome is at war with the city of Alba Longa. To end it, each side chooses three brothers to fight to the death.

slides.headline: The oath
slides.text: For Rome: the three Horatii brothers. Arms stretched out, they swear to win or die. Not one of them hesitates.

slides.headline: Three swords
slides.text: Their father raises the three swords. Look closely: two are curved, one is straight. Some see a hint that only one will survive.

slides.headline: The women
slides.text: On the right, the women collapse in grief. They are not only afraid for the brothers. Their pain is more complicated than that.

slides.headline: Camilla
slides.text: Camilla, the brothers' sister, is engaged to one of the enemy brothers. Whatever happens tomorrow, she will lose someone she loves.

slides.headline: Sabina
slides.text: Next to her, Sabina is a sister of the enemy brothers, married to one of the Horatii. Her family will kill her family.

slides.headline: The children
slides.text: Behind them, the children cling to the women. One child hides her face, as if she already understands what this oath means.

slides.headline: After the oath
slides.text: The moment is David's own invention. In the legend, one brother survives, then kills Camilla for weeping. Duty or family?
